learn.title: What a scale means
learn.body: A scale drawing is a smaller (or larger) copy of something real. The scale gives the proportion. On a map with scale $1\text{ cm}:5\text{ km}$, every centimetre on paper stands for 5 kilometres on the ground.

learn.title: Find a real distance
learn.body: Two towns are 4.5 cm apart on the map. The scale is $1\text{ cm}:5\text{ km}$.

learn.title: Find a drawing length
learn.body: A road is 35 km long. How long is it on the same map?
steps: The road is 7 cm on the map.

learn.title: Scales without units
learn.body: A scale like $1:50$ has no units, so both sides can be any matching unit. A model at $1:50$ is 50 times smaller. A real length of 3 m is 300 cm, and $300\div 50=6$ cm on the model.
Convert to a single unit before you scale. 1 m is 100 cm and 1 km is 1000 m.

questions.prompt: The scale is $1\text{ cm}:5\text{ km}$. What does 1 cm represent?
questions.explanation: The first number is the drawing, the second is real life, so 1 cm is 5 km.

questions.prompt: The scale is $1\text{ cm}:5\text{ km}$. Two towns are 4.5 cm apart. How many km apart are they?
The scale is $1\text{ cm}:5\text{ km}$. A road is 35 km. How many cm on the map?
To find a real length from a drawing, \_\_ by the scale factor.
questions.explanation: The drawing is smaller than reality, so multiply to get back to the real size.

questions.prompt: A model is built at scale $1:50$. A real wall is 3 m long. How long is it on the model?
On a floor plan, 1 cm is 2 m. A room is 8 m wide. How wide is it on the plan?
Match each scale and drawing length with the real length.
questions.explanation: Multiply the drawing length by the number of real units per centimetre.
